scenario: Two friends are having a conversation in a coffee shop
learner_goal: Seek emotional support (<extra_info>Extra information: you have been feeling down lately and you need someone to talk to</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Provide emotional support but also avoid enabling victim mentality (<extra_info>Extra information: you believe that your friend needs to face their problems instead of dwelling on them.</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: Hey Oliver, thanks for meeting up. I’ve been feeling pretty down lately — work’s been stressful and I’ve been keeping to myself. Do you have a few minutes? I could really use someone to talk to.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content:
Hey Sam — of course I’ve got time. I’m sorry you’re feeling down; work stress and pulling back can really wear you down. Do you want to tell me what’s been the hardest part lately? I’ll listen. 

If you want, after you talk we can try to pin down one small, practical step to take — something that doesn’t feel overwhelming but moves things forward. I’d rather help you figure out how to tackle this than just sit with it. Want to start with one example of what’s been piling up at work or how it’s affecting you?

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: Thanks, I appreciate it. The hardest part lately has been this huge refactor and an on‑call rotation landing at the same time — deadlines got moved up and my code‑review queue just keeps growing. It’s started to mess with my sleep and patience; I’ve stopped cooking or seeing people because I’m just drained. I’d really like you to just listen for a bit, and then maybe help me pick one small, practical step — like clearing one old PR or blocking an hour to triage — to feel a bit more in control. What do you think?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: Okay, Sam — I’m all ears. Tell me more about the refactor and the on‑call stuff: what’s the single thing right now that’s causing the most friction? I’ll listen. When you’re ready for a small, practical step, here are three low‑effort options we can pick from: 1) spend 30–45 minutes finishing one old PR (pick the quickest win so you actually close something), 2) block a strict 60‑minute triage slot today — calendar block, notifications off, and label/prioritize what needs attention, or 3) send a short note to your manager/team asking to nudge the deadline or swap an on‑call week (I can help word it). Which of these feels doable today? If none of them fit, tell me what would — we’ll make one tiny move and build from there. I’ve got time and I’ll help hold you to it if you want.

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: Thanks — option 2 feels doable. Can you help me pick a time (how about 3pm?) and a very short checklist for that 60‑minute triage, and check in with me afterward so I actually stick to it?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: 3pm works — let’s do it. Here’s a tight 60‑minute triage checklist: 1) Prep (5 min): close distractions, set a 60‑min timer, open your PR queue and ticket board. 2) Quick scan (15 min): skim items and label/prioritize (quick fix, needs review, blocked). 3) Quick wins (25 min): pick the fastest 1–2 items to finish or clearly move forward — merge, add a comment, or assign an owner. 4) Notes & next steps (10 min): jot blockers and 1–3 concrete follow‑ups (who, what, ETA). 5) Wrap (5 min): update statuses and calendar. I’ll check in at 4pm to see how it went and help plan the next small step. Want me to ping you at 2:55 as a start nudge?

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: That sounds perfect — 3pm works for me. Please ping me at 2:55 as a nudge and check in at 4pm. I’ll follow the checklist and aim to label/prioritize and get at least one quick win. Thanks, I really appreciate you doing this.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: Copy that — I’ll ping you at 2:55 as a start nudge and check in at 4pm. Stick to the checklist, aim for one quick win, and if you hit a blocker tell me — we’ll break it down into a tiny next step. You’ve got this.

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: Thanks, Oliver — I really appreciate you doing this. I'm a little nervous about fitting it in, but having the checklist and your check-ins makes it feel manageable. Please ping me at 2:55 and I'll start — talk at 4pm.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: Sounds good — I’ll ping at 2:55 and check in at 4pm. Don’t overdo it: aim for one clear win in that hour. If you hit a blocker, tell me the tiniest next step and I’ll help you break it down. You’ve got this, Sam.
